Traupman 288

Andresian p. 21

violoncellum, violoncellī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

The Italian name in Latin dress, like violīnum (see violin). Andresian writes viōloncellum; no source marks a long o, and Traupman leaves it unmarked.

Other words

  • fidēs majōrēs

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. strings3: cello (Rauch, 1641)

    “The larger strings”: fidēs, plural, is the classical word for a stringed instrument (Cic.).

  • fidēs crūrālēs

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. strings3: cello

    “Leg strings”, the instrument held between the knees.

See also violin, musical instrument, viola, double bass, orchestra.
